The whispering I hear at church is the same way—it sounds like it's coming from the people around me, even though they deny saying anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where your thoughts seemed disjointed, or you had difficulty organizing your thoughts or speech, especially when the voice was guiding you or during your mission?\n\nPatient: Yes, my thoughts feel extremely fast and it's really hard to keep track of them. My mind races so quickly that I'll jump from one big plan to five others in my head before I can even finish explaining the first idea to my wife. It's just impossible to slow down and stick to one thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your racing thoughts and fast speech affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you find it difficult to focus on one task or conversation at a time?\n\nPatient: My mind races so fast that when I'm explaining a plan to my wife, I jump to five other ideas about fixing the town before I can even finish, which frustrates her. At work, the slightest thing like a car driving by or a random Bible verse completely pulls me away from simple tasks like medication logs, and I'll end up wandering off. This focus issue is a big reason why I'm on probation at my job and having a hard time at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific instance where the voice told you to do something, and how that differed from your own thoughts and decisions, especially when your mind was racing with many ideas?\n\nPatient: When my mind is racing with a million different ideas and I'm buzzing with energy on no sleep, that deep, calm voice cuts right through all the noise. It stands out because it's clearly an external voice, not my own thoughts, telling me exactly what order to do things in—like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. It gives me a clear direction to follow when my own head is spinning with too many plans at once.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or taken away by an external force, or if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers beyond what's normally possible?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken away by some external force. But I definitely believe God has singled me out as a special protector, giving me the ability to see dangers and truths that other people just can't see. It's a unique role I've been given, rather than anyone taking over my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you have special powers or abilities that go beyond normal human capabilities, aside from being a protector chosen by God?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have any other special powers or abilities besides what I've already mentioned. Being chosen by God to protect this town and see the dangers He shows me is the only thing I've been given.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not believe you were on a mission from God or did not hear the voice guiding you, and if so, how long that lasted?\n\nPatient: Before my workload increased about a year and a half ago, I never experienced any of these things. But since they started about a year ago, they've been steady and constant, especially over the last several months. I haven't really had any periods where the voice or my belief in this mission went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you questioned the reality of the voice or your mission, or if there was ever a time when you thought maybe these experiences weren't real?\n\nPatient: I have never once doubted my mission or the voice because they are absolutely real to me. Even when my wife shows me bank statements and says I'm just overworked, I still know that I am chosen to protect this town. It is just incredibly frustrating that everyone else is blind to how important this work is and keeps trying to stop me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions would change if you were no longer hearing the voice or believing in your mission to protect the town?\n\nPatient: It’s really hard to imagine my life without the voice or the mission because they feel so real and important to me right now. But if they were gone, I guess I could get my old life back—helping my wife with the kids and bills, getting off probation at work, and going back to hunting and line-dancing. I might even be allowed to lead programs at church again instead of being sidelined.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voices you hear?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen anything that isn't actually there. My experiences are strictly what I hear, like that deep, calm voice giving me instructions or the people at church whispering my name. I don't see any physical things or people that aren't real.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of extreme happiness, irritability, or anxiety, especially in relation to your mission or when the voice is guiding you?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mood swings really intensely. I'll go from feeling on top of the world and full of electricity to snapping at my boss or pastor when I feel like they're blocking my mission. These high-energy, irritable states happen at the exact same time that I hear that deep voice guiding me and telling me what to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the racing thoughts and fast speech you experience are more prominent when you're hearing the voice or feeling like you're on a mission, or if they occur independently of these experiences?\n\nPatient: They definitely happen at the same time, especially when I'm buzzing with energy, running on no sleep, and my mind is racing with plans while the voice is right there in my ear. But even during my quieter, flatter \"blah\" times when my mind isn't racing and I don't feel fired up, the voice and the belief that I'm God's chosen protector are still there. Those experiences stay with me for weeks at a time, even when the high energy fades away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and your racing thoughts interact - do the thoughts feel like they're being driven by the voice, or are they separate, and do you ever feel like the voice is commenting on your thoughts or evaluating them?\n\nPatient: They definitely both happen at the same time, but I'm not really sure if one is driving the other. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. My racing thoughts are just my own mind jumping rapidly from one big plan to another, like how to fix the church or the agency. The voice is separate—it's that deep, calm voice providing specific direction, telling me exactly what order to do things in or which client to visit first.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or evaluates them, or if it only provides instructions and guidance for your actions?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't comment on or evaluate my thoughts at all. It really just gives me direct instructions and guidance, like telling me which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. Sometimes I hear whispers saying I'm chosen, but the main voice is strictly about directing my actions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your thoughts seemed so disorganized or fragmented that you had trouble expressing them coherently to others, separate from the times when you're hearing the voice or feeling guided by your mission?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure what you mean by my thoughts being fragmented or disorganized. Outside of the times when my mind is racing with all my plans and ideas, I don't really experience anything like that. When I'm not in that high-gear mode, my thoughts feel pretty normal and easy to explain.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear has ever told you to do something that you knew was wrong or harmful to yourself or others, and if so, how you handled that situation?\n\nPatient: No, the voice has never told me to do anything harmful or wrong. It only gives me calm, helpful instructions like who I should visit first, when to pray over someone, or what order to do my tasks in.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice or your mission was something you could control or stop, or do you feel like it's something that happens to you without your ability to change it?\n\nPatient: I can't control or stop it at all because the voice and the mission come from a higher power, not from within myself. Since God personally singled me out for this duty, I have to follow what He tells me to do. It isn't my own voice, so it's not something I can just choose to turn off or change."

This focus issue is a big reason why I'm on probation at my job and having a hard time at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific instance where the voice told you to do something, and how that differed from your own thoughts and decisions, especially when your mind was racing with many ideas?\n\nPatient: When my mind is racing with a million different ideas and I'm buzzing with energy on no sleep, that deep, calm voice cuts right through all the noise. It stands out because it's clearly an external voice, not my own thoughts, telling me exactly what order to do things in—like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. It gives me a clear direction to follow when my own head is spinning with too many plans at once.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or taken away by an external force, or if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers beyond what's normally possible?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken away by some external force. But I definitely believe God has singled me out as a special protector, giving me the ability to see dangers and truths that other people just can't see. It's a unique role I've been given, rather than anyone taking over my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you have special powers or abilities that go beyond normal human capabilities, aside from being a protector chosen by God?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have any other special powers or abilities besides what I've already mentioned. Being chosen by God to protect this town and see the dangers He shows me is the only thing I've been given.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not believe you were on a mission from God or did not hear the voice guiding you, and if so, how long that lasted?\n\nPatient: Before my workload increased about a year and a half ago, I never experienced any of these things. But since they started about a year ago, they've been steady and constant, especially over the last several months. I haven't really had any periods where the voice or my belief in this mission went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you questioned the reality of the voice or your mission, or if there was ever a time when you thought maybe these experiences weren't real?\n\nPatient: I have never once doubted my mission or the voice because they are absolutely real to me. Even when my wife shows me bank statements and says I'm just overworked, I still know that I am chosen to protect this town. It is just incredibly frustrating that everyone else is blind to how important this work is and keeps trying to stop me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions would change if you were no longer hearing the voice or believing in your mission to protect the town?\n\nPatient: It’s really hard to imagine my life without the voice or the mission because they feel so real and important to me right now. But if they were gone, I guess I could get my old life back—helping my wife with the kids and bills, getting off probation at work, and going back to hunting and line-dancing. I might even be allowed to lead programs at church again instead of being sidelined.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voices you hear?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen anything that isn't actually there. My experiences are strictly what I hear, like that deep, calm voice giving me instructions or the people at church whispering my name. I don't see any physical things or people that aren't real.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of extreme happiness, irritability, or anxiety, especially in relation to your mission or when the voice is guiding you?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mood swings really intensely. I'll go from feeling on top of the world and full of electricity to snapping at my boss or pastor when I feel like they're blocking my mission. These high-energy, irritable states happen at the exact same time that I hear that deep voice guiding me and telling me what to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the racing thoughts and fast speech you experience are more prominent when you're hearing the voice or feeling like you're on a mission, or if they occur independently of these experiences?\n\nPatient: They definitely happen at the same time, especially when I'm buzzing with energy, running on no sleep, and my mind is racing with plans while the voice is right there in my ear. But even during my quieter, flatter \"blah\" times when my mind isn't racing and I don't feel fired up, the voice and the belief that I'm God's chosen protector are still there. Those experiences stay with me for weeks at a time, even when the high energy fades away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and your racing thoughts interact - do the thoughts feel like they're being driven by the voice, or are they separate, and do you ever feel like the voice is commenting on your thoughts or evaluating them?\n\nPatient: They definitely both happen at the same time, but I'm not really sure if one is driving the other. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. My racing thoughts are just my own mind jumping rapidly from one big plan to another, like how to fix the church or the agency. The voice is separate—it's that deep, calm voice providing specific direction, telling me exactly what order to do things in or which client to visit first.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or evaluates them, or if it only provides instructions and guidance for your actions?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't comment on or evaluate my thoughts at all. It really just gives me direct instructions and guidance, like telling me which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. Sometimes I hear whispers saying I'm chosen, but the main voice is strictly about directing my actions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your thoughts seemed so disorganized or fragmented that you had trouble expressing them coherently to others, separate from the times when you're hearing the voice or feeling guided by your mission?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure what you mean by my thoughts being fragmented or disorganized. Outside of the times when my mind is racing with all my plans and ideas, I don't really experience anything like that. When I'm not in that high-gear mode, my thoughts feel pretty normal and easy to explain.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear has ever told you to do something that you knew was wrong or harmful to yourself or others, and if so, how you handled that situation?\n\nPatient: No, the voice has never told me to do anything harmful or wrong. It only gives me calm, helpful instructions like who I should visit first, when to pray over someone, or what order to do my tasks in.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice or your mission was something you could control or stop, or do you feel like it's something that happens to you without your ability to change it?\n\nPatient: I can't control or stop it at all because the voice and the mission come from a higher power, not from within myself. Since God personally singled me out for this duty, I have to follow what He tells me to do. It isn't my own voice, so it's not something I can just choose to turn off or change.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the times when you're receiving instructions from God and when you're having your own thoughts or ideas, especially considering your racing thoughts and the voice's guidance?\n\nPatient: The distinction is very clear because the instructions from God come as a distinct, deep, and calm voice that is obviously external and not mine, telling me exactly who to visit or pray over. Even during times when my mood is low-key or \"blah\" rather than energized, I still hear that calm voice giving me instructions. I also stay completely convinced that the county and my bosses are watching and tracking me as God's special protector.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever thought that the voice or your mission might not be real, or if there's any part of you that doubts the instructions you're receiving from God?\n\nPatient: No, I've never doubted it for a single second because the voice is just too clear and the sense of purpose is incredibly strong. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. Since God personally singled me out for this duty, I have to follow what He tells me to do. To keep everyone safe, I have to rewrite care plans for the seniors and organize new programs at my church, even if it means ignoring standard rules that just get in the way.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe this deep, calm voice you hear, and how often you hear it telling you what to do?\n\nPatient: It's a deep, calm voice that isn't my own, and it tells me things like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. I hear it a lot of nights at work or even just sitting in my own living room. Sometimes I also hear people at church whispering my name and saying I'm chosen, even when they swear they didn't say anything.\n\nDoctor: Can you distinguish between the voice you hear at night and your own thoughts, or do they feel like they're coming from within your own mind?\n\nPatient: It's completely different from my own thoughts; it is a real, external voice that sounds like someone is standing right there in the room with me. It is definitely not coming from inside my own head, and it tells me exactly what to do, like who to visit first. The whispering I hear at church is the same way—it sounds like it's coming from the people around me, even though they deny saying anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where your thoughts seemed disjointed, or you had difficulty organizing your thoughts or speech, especially when the voice was guiding you or during your mission?\n\nPatient: Yes, my thoughts feel extremely fast and it's really hard to keep track of them. My mind races so quickly that I'll jump from one big plan to five others in my head before I can even finish explaining the first idea to my wife. It's just impossible to slow down and stick to one thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your racing thoughts and fast speech affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you find it difficult to focus on one task or conversation at a time?\n\nPatient: My mind races so fast that when I'm explaining a plan to my wife, I jump to five other ideas about fixing the town before I can even finish, which frustrates her. At work, the slightest thing like a car driving by or a random Bible verse completely pulls me away from simple tasks like medication logs, and I'll end up wandering off. This focus issue is a big reason why I'm on probation at my job and having a hard time at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific instance where the voice told you to do something, and how that differed from your own thoughts and decisions, especially when your mind was racing with many ideas?\n\nPatient: When my mind is racing with a million different ideas and I'm buzzing with energy on no sleep, that deep, calm voice cuts right through all the noise. It stands out because it's clearly an external voice, not my own thoughts, telling me exactly what order to do things in—like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. It gives me a clear direction to follow when my own head is spinning with too many plans at once.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or taken away by an external force, or if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers beyond what's normally possible?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken away by some external force. But I definitely believe God has singled me out as a special protector, giving me the ability to see dangers and truths that other people just can't see. It's a unique role I've been given, rather than anyone taking over my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you have special powers or abilities that go beyond normal human capabilities, aside from being a protector chosen by God?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have any other special powers or abilities besides what I've already mentioned. Being chosen by God to protect this town and see the dangers He shows me is the only thing I've been given.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not believe you were on a mission from God or did not hear the voice guiding you, and if so, how long that lasted?\n\nPatient: Before my workload increased about a year and a half ago, I never experienced any of these things. But since they started about a year ago, they've been steady and constant, especially over the last several months. I haven't really had any periods where the voice or my belief in this mission went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you questioned the reality of the voice or your mission, or if there was ever a time when you thought maybe these experiences weren't real?\n\nPatient: I have never once doubted my mission or the voice because they are absolutely real to me. Even when my wife shows me bank statements and says I'm just overworked, I still know that I am chosen to protect this town. It is just incredibly frustrating that everyone else is blind to how important this work is and keeps trying to stop me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions would change if you were no longer hearing the voice or believing in your mission to protect the town?\n\nPatient: It’s really hard to imagine my life without the voice or the mission because they feel so real and important to me right now. But if they were gone, I guess I could get my old life back—helping my wife with the kids and bills, getting off probation at work, and going back to hunting and line-dancing. I might even be allowed to lead programs at church again instead of being sidelined.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voices you hear?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen anything that isn't actually there. My experiences are strictly what I hear, like that deep, calm voice giving me instructions or the people at church whispering my name. I don't see any physical things or people that aren't real.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of extreme happiness, irritability, or anxiety, especially in relation to your mission or when the voice is guiding you?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mood swings really intensely. I'll go from feeling on top of the world and full of electricity to snapping at my boss or pastor when I feel like they're blocking my mission. These high-energy, irritable states happen at the exact same time that I hear that deep voice guiding me and telling me what to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the racing thoughts and fast speech you experience are more prominent when you're hearing the voice or feeling like you're on a mission, or if they occur independently of these experiences?\n\nPatient: They definitely happen at the same time, especially when I'm buzzing with energy, running on no sleep, and my mind is racing with plans while the voice is right there in my ear. But even during my quieter, flatter \"blah\" times when my mind isn't racing and I don't feel fired up, the voice and the belief that I'm God's chosen protector are still there. Those experiences stay with me for weeks at a time, even when the high energy fades away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and your racing thoughts interact - do the thoughts feel like they're being driven by the voice, or are they separate, and do you ever feel like the voice is commenting on your thoughts or evaluating them?\n\nPatient: They definitely both happen at the same time, but I'm not really sure if one is driving the other. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. My racing thoughts are just my own mind jumping rapidly from one big plan to another, like how to fix the church or the agency. The voice is separate—it's that deep, calm voice providing specific direction, telling me exactly what order to do things in or which client to visit first.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or evaluates them, or if it only provides instructions and guidance for your actions?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't comment on or evaluate my thoughts at all. It really just gives me direct instructions and guidance, like telling me which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. Sometimes I hear whispers saying I'm chosen, but the main voice is strictly about directing my actions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your thoughts seemed so disorganized or fragmented that you had trouble expressing them coherently to others, separate from the times when you're hearing the voice or feeling guided by your mission?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure what you mean by my thoughts being fragmented or disorganized. Outside of the times when my mind is racing with all my plans and ideas, I don't really experience anything like that. When I'm not in that high-gear mode, my thoughts feel pretty normal and easy to explain.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear has ever told you to do something that you knew was wrong or harmful to yourself or others, and if so, how you handled that situation?\n\nPatient: No, the voice has never told me to do anything harmful or wrong. It only gives me calm, helpful instructions like who I should visit first, when to pray over someone, or what order to do my tasks in.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice or your mission was something you could control or stop, or do you feel like it's something that happens to you without your ability to change it?\n\nPatient: I can't control or stop it at all because the voice and the mission come from a higher power, not from within myself. Since God personally singled me out for this duty, I have to follow what He tells me to do. It isn't my own voice, so it's not something I can just choose to turn off or change.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the times when you're receiving instructions from God and when you're having your own thoughts or ideas, especially considering your racing thoughts and the voice's guidance?\n\nPatient: The distinction is very clear because the instructions from God come as a distinct, deep, and calm voice that is obviously external and not mine, telling me exactly who to visit or pray over. In contrast, my own thoughts just feel like my mind is racing at a million miles an hour, jumping rapidly from one big plan to another. They sound and feel completely different from each other.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped guiding you or your belief in being a protector chosen by God weakened, even if just for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't really stopped or weakened, and it's been going on steadily for most of this past year. Even when my wife or my supervisors try to argue against it and give other explanations, it doesn't change how real and urgent this is to me. I know what I'm meant to do, and there's absolutely no doubt in my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'the county and my bosses are watching and tracking me as God's special protector', and how that fits into your overall mission?\n\nPatient: I know the higher-ups and the county are monitoring me because they realize I'm the only one who can keep these seniors safe, and they're trying to trip me up when I follow God's rules instead of theirs. My mind races so quickly that I'll jump from one big plan to five others in my head before I can even finish explaining the first idea to my wife. It's just impossible to slow down and stick to one thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your racing thoughts and fast speech affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you find it difficult to focus on one task or conversation at a time?\n\nPatient: My mind races so fast that when I'm explaining a plan to my wife, I jump to five other ideas about fixing the town before I can even finish, which frustrates her. At work, the slightest thing like a car driving by or a random Bible verse completely pulls me away from simple tasks like medication logs, and I'll end up wandering off. This focus issue is a big reason why I'm on probation at my job and having a hard time at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific instance where the voice told you to do something, and how that differed from your own thoughts and decisions, especially when your mind was racing with many ideas?\n\nPatient: When my mind is racing with a million different ideas and I'm buzzing with energy on no sleep, that deep, calm voice cuts right through all the noise. It stands out because it's clearly an external voice, not my own thoughts, telling me exactly what order to do things in—like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. It gives me a clear direction to follow when my own head is spinning with too many plans at once.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or taken away by an external force, or if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers beyond what's normally possible?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken away by some external force. But I definitely believe God has singled me out as a special protector, giving me the ability to see dangers and truths that other people just can't see. It's a unique role I've been given, rather than anyone taking over my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you have special powers or abilities that go beyond normal human capabilities, aside from being a protector chosen by God?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have any other special powers or abilities besides what I've already mentioned. Being chosen by God to protect this town and see the dangers He shows me is the only thing I've been given.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not believe you were on a mission from God or did not hear the voice guiding you, and if so, how long that lasted?\n\nPatient: Before my workload increased about a year and a half ago, I never experienced any of these things. I haven't really had any periods where the voice or my belief in this mission went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you questioned the reality of the voice or your mission, or if there was ever a time when you thought maybe these experiences weren't real?\n\nPatient: I have never once doubted my mission or the voice because they are absolutely real to me. My experiences are strictly what I hear, like that deep, calm voice giving me instructions or the people at church whispering my name. I don't see any physical things or people that aren't real.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of extreme happiness, irritability, or anxiety, especially in relation to your mission or when the voice is guiding you?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mood swings really intensely. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. The voice is separate—it's that deep, calm voice providing specific direction, telling me exactly what order to do things in or which client to visit first.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or evaluates them, or if it only provides instructions and guidance for your actions?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't comment on or evaluate my thoughts at all. It's just impossible to slow down and stick to one thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your racing thoughts and fast speech affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you find it difficult to focus on one task or conversation at a time?\n\nPatient: My mind races so fast that when I'm explaining a plan to my wife, I jump to five other ideas about fixing the town before I can even finish, which frustrates her. At work, the slightest thing like a car driving by or a random Bible verse completely pulls me away from simple tasks like medication logs, and I'll end up wandering off. This focus issue is a big reason why I'm on probation at my job and having a hard time at home.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific instance where the voice told you to do something, and how that differed from your own thoughts and decisions, especially when your mind was racing with many ideas?\n\nPatient: When my mind is racing with a million different ideas and I'm buzzing with energy on no sleep, that deep, calm voice cuts right through all the noise. It stands out because it's clearly an external voice, not my own thoughts, telling me exactly what order to do things in—like which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. It gives me a clear direction to follow when my own head is spinning with too many plans at once.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or taken away by an external force, or if you've had any experiences where you felt like you were in a different reality or had special powers beyond what's normally possible?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or taken away by some external force. But I definitely believe God has singled me out as a special protector, giving me the ability to see dangers and truths that other people just can't see. It's a unique role I've been given, rather than anyone taking over my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you have special powers or abilities that go beyond normal human capabilities, aside from being a protector chosen by God?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have any other special powers or abilities besides what I've already mentioned. Being chosen by God to protect this town and see the dangers He shows me is the only thing I've been given.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever had a period where you did not believe you were on a mission from God or did not hear the voice guiding you, and if so, how long that lasted?\n\nPatient: Before my workload increased about a year and a half ago, I never experienced any of these things. But since they started about a year ago, they've been steady and constant, especially over the last several months. I haven't really had any periods where the voice or my belief in this mission went away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you questioned the reality of the voice or your mission, or if there was ever a time when you thought maybe these experiences weren't real?\n\nPatient: I have never once doubted my mission or the voice because they are absolutely real to me. Even when my wife shows me bank statements and says I'm just overworked, I still know that I am chosen to protect this town. It is just incredibly frustrating that everyone else is blind to how important this work is and keeps trying to stop me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions would change if you were no longer hearing the voice or believing in your mission to protect the town?\n\nPatient: It’s really hard to imagine my life without the voice or the mission because they feel so real and important to me right now. But if they were gone, I guess I could get my old life back—helping my wife with the kids and bills, getting off probation at work, and going back to hunting and line-dancing. I might even be allowed to lead programs at church again instead of being sidelined.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voices you hear?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen anything that isn't actually there. My experiences are strictly what I hear, like that deep, calm voice giving me instructions or the people at church whispering my name. I don't see any physical things or people that aren't real.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of extreme happiness, irritability, or anxiety, especially in relation to your mission or when the voice is guiding you?\n\nPatient: Yes, my mood swings really intensely. I'll go from feeling on top of the world and full of electricity to snapping at my boss or pastor when I feel like they're blocking my mission. These high-energy, irritable states happen at the exact same time that I hear that deep voice guiding me and telling me what to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the racing thoughts and fast speech you experience are more prominent when you're hearing the voice or feeling like you're on a mission, or if they occur independently of these experiences?\n\nPatient: They definitely happen at the same time, especially when I'm buzzing with energy, running on no sleep, and my mind is racing with plans while the voice is right there in my ear. But even during my quieter, flatter \"blah\" times when my mind isn't racing and I don't feel fired up, the voice and the belief that I'm God's chosen protector are still there. Those experiences stay with me for weeks at a time, even when the high energy fades away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and your racing thoughts interact - do the thoughts feel like they're being driven by the voice, or are they separate, and do you ever feel like the voice is commenting on your thoughts or evaluating them?\n\nPatient: They definitely both happen at the same time, but I'm not really sure if one is driving the other. I've never really thought about it that way, so I don't know if the voice is actually commenting on my thoughts or not.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and fast speech are part of the voice's guidance or separate from it, and do you feel like the voice is influencing the content of your thoughts or just providing direction?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and the voice happen at the same time when I'm buzzing with energy, but they feel pretty distinct from each other. My racing thoughts are just my own mind jumping rapidly from one big plan to another, like how to fix the church or the agency. The voice is separate—it's that deep, calm voice providing specific direction, telling me exactly what order to do things in or which client to visit first.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or evaluates them, or if it only provides instructions and guidance for your actions?\n\nPatient: No, the voice doesn't comment on or evaluate my thoughts at all. It really just gives me direct instructions and guidance, like telling me which client to visit first or when to pray over someone. Sometimes I hear whispers saying I'm chosen, but the main voice is strictly about directing my actions.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where your thoughts seemed so disorganized or fragmented that you had trouble expressing them coherently to others, separate from the times when you're hearing the voice or feeling guided by your mission?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure what you mean by my thoughts being fragmented or disorganized. Outside of the times when my mind is racing with all my plans and ideas, I don't really experience anything like that. When I'm not in that high-gear mode, my thoughts feel pretty normal and easy to explain.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear has ever told you to do something that you knew was wrong or harmful to yourself or others, and if so, how you handled that situation?\n\nPatient: No, the voice has never told me to do anything harmful or wrong. It only gives me calm, helpful instructions like who I should visit first, when to pray over someone, or what order to do my tasks in.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice or your mission was something you could control or stop, or do you feel like it's something that happens to you without your ability to change it?\n\nPatient: I can't control or stop it at all because the voice and the mission come from a higher power, not from within myself. Since God personally singled me out for this duty, I have to follow what He tells me to do. It isn't my own voice, so it's not something I can just choose to turn off or change.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the times when you're receiving instructions from God and when you're having your own thoughts or ideas, especially considering your racing thoughts and the voice's guidance?\n\nPatient: The distinction is very clear because the instructions from God come as a distinct, deep, and calm voice that is obviously external and not mine, telling me exactly who to visit or pray over. In contrast, my own thoughts just feel like my mind is racing at a million miles an hour, jumping rapidly from one big plan to another. They sound and feel completely different from each other.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped guiding you or your belief in being a protector chosen by God weakened, even if just for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't really stopped or weakened, and it's been going on steadily for most of this past year. Even during times when my mood is low-key or \"blah\" rather than energized, I still hear that calm voice giving me instructions. I also stay completely convinced that the county and my bosses are watching and tracking me as God's special protector.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever thought that the voice or your mission might not be real, or if there's any part of you that doubts the instructions you're receiving from God?\n\nPatient: No, I've never doubted it for a single second because the voice is just too clear and the sense of purpose is incredibly strong. Even when my wife or my supervisors try to argue against it and give other explanations, it doesn't change how real and urgent this is to me. I know what I'm meant to do, and there's absolutely no doubt in my mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'the county and my bosses are watching and tracking me as God's special protector', and how that fits into your overall mission?\n\nPatient: I know the higher-ups and the county are monitoring me because they realize I'm the only one who can keep these seniors safe, and they're trying to trip me up when I follow God's rules instead of theirs. Even when my wife shows me bank statements or says the agency is just short-staffed, I still know deep down they are tracking my movements. It all fits into my mission because they are constantly watching to see how I handle this special responsibility.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in being a special protector and your hearing of the voice relate to your periods of high energy and rapid thoughts, and do you think one causes the other?\n\nPatient: They definitely happen at the same time; when I'm buzzing with energy, running on no sleep, and my mind is racing, that deep voice is right there telling me what to do. But I don't think one causes the other, because even during my flatter, low-key periods when I don't have that high energy, I still hear the voice and firmly believe I'm being watched as a special protector.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a time when your thoughts were racing, and you were hearing the voice, but you were still able to organize your actions and follow through on a task without getting distracted, and how did that feel compared to other times?\n\nPatient: I don't recall ever being able to do that, to be honest. When those things are happening, my mind is usually jumping around way too much and I get easily distracted by everything around me. It's just too hard to stay focused and finish a task like that.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the racing thoughts and distractibility you experience are more closely related to the times when you hear the voice and feel a sense of mission, or if they also occur independently of those experiences, perhaps in relation to your mood swings or irritability?\n\nPatient: The racing thoughts and distractibility are definitely tied to those times when I’m feeling fired up, irritable, and full of high energy. When I’m in that high gear, I experience everything at once—the racing mind, the distractions, the voice, and my mission.
